scope.flow: limit order append to existing price level, then cancellation/full fill/expiry removal
scope.environment: on-chain order book contract with doubly-linked per-price-level order list
evidence: Every time a limit order is appended to an existing price-level, the contract fails to persist the new order’s `prevOrderId` field. Subsequent cancellation, full fill, or expiry of that appended order causes the removal routine to mis-handle the doubly-linked list, detaching all earlier orders at that price.
Order stored without links. `_updateBookPostOrder()` writes the freshly created `Order` struct to `storage`; `prevOrderId` is still `0`.
Because `order` is a memory copy, the storage slot at `self.orders[order.id]` never receives the new `prevOrderId`.

Here, `if (!prev.isNull()) … else limit.headOrder = next;` treats the order as a head (since `prev == 0`). It rewires `limit.headOrder` to `next`, effectively dropping the true head segment from the list. Those older orders become unreachable.
